bio.text: Detz is a Wolverhampton producer formerly known as Detonator. He started out making grime instrumentals. He has pursued his own instrumental work alongside production for MCs, from the Indian Summers EP in 2016 to his first album, Sometimes, I Hate Myself, in 2019.

bio.text: Dubzy is a grime MC who grew up between London and Derby and started rapping at thirteen. In 2013 he represented Derby in a SPITFIRE freestyle for JDZmedia. A year later, on his mixtape Gift of the Gab, he traded verses with Eyez on ‘Say My Name’, brought JakMan and Directs together on ‘Snazz 4 Life’, and opened the tape with Trim.

Snazz was also the name of his clothing brand. By 2015 his team was supplying headwear to KA. That year he travelled from Derby to London for Red Bull Studios’ Raise the Bar, writing verses on the journey for a session with producer Z-Dot. When Eyez brought MCs from the Midlands and the North together for Mind the Gap in 2016, he chose Dubzy to represent Derby.

In 2019 Dubzy used the video for ‘What You Telling Me’ to reintroduce himself. Filmed around London, it moves between time with friends and family and a political message. Dubzy described those scenes as different parts of his own life.

bio.text: Eyez wrote his first bars, recorded his first tune and had his first clash in Derby. He started rapping at about eleven, trying to keep up with his brothers. In an interview he traced his ear for lyrics to the US hip-hop he listened to as a kid, though grime was where he first felt at home writing. His SPITFIRE freestyles for JDZmedia helped him find an audience beyond the city.

In 2016 Eyez put together Mind the Gap with Red Bull. He wanted listeners to hear MCs who were already rated in their own cities. His picks included Dubzy for Derby, Mez for Nottingham and Dialect for Leeds. That year he also captained Derby in Grime-A-Side, taking on Jaykae’s Birmingham team on the way to a win over Leicester in the final. In 2017 he went back to football in a different role, joining Derby County’s RamsTV as a host.

bio.text: Jaykae came up in Birmingham through grime clashes, pirate radio and the crew Invasion Alert. He remembers MCs trading freestyles on the city’s Grime Blog YouTube channel in 2009, then watching to see whose response drew the biggest crowd. On radio he shared the mic with Rusky, Remtrex and RM alongside DJ Free before getting a show on Birmingham station Silk City.

Clashing shaped his choices as a captain in Red Bull’s Grime-A-Side in 2016. He picked Deadly and Mayhem for Birmingham because he had seen them take on anyone at a set. They faced Eyez’s Derby team in the quarter-final. For his solo comeback, Jaykae worked with producer Thomas Mellor on ‘Toothache’. He told Wonderland the title came from an actual toothache he had while writing it.

bio.text: S-X is a producer, singer and songwriter from Wolverhampton. As a teenager he made beats on his home computer and travelled to the BBC studios hoping to get them into the hands of DJs Tim Westwood and Ras Kwame. He was still at school when grime MCs picked up his ‘Woo Riddim’. By eighteen he had worked with Chipmunk, Tinie Tempah and Skepta.

After a spell working in the Wolverhampton Wanderers warehouse, S-X began putting his own voice on record. He dates his start as a singer to 2017. The move took him from supplying beats for other people’s bars to touring songs he had written himself. In 2022 he released his debut solo album, Things Change.
